title: Shielded Zcash Deposits Are Now Available on Gemini
summary: Gemini customers can now deposit their Zcash via shielded addresses.
body_markdown:
For the first time, Gemini customers can now deposit Zcash (ZEC) to a shielded Unified Address on Gemini Exchange. Simply copy your Gemini-issued address into a compatible Zcash wallet, send, and your funds stay shielded throughout the transfer.


Gemini launched shielded Zcash withdrawals this summer. Today, shielded deposits close the loop, helping make Gemini the first major exchange globally to have both available. ZEC can now move into and out of Gemini with privacy on the public blockchain, from start to finish.


If your wallet needs a transparent address, that option is still there. Shielded is the default.


### How It Works


Open the ZEC deposit flow on Gemini Exchange. You will see a shielded Unified Address, issued by Gemini. Copy it into your compatible Zcash wallet and send your ZEC.


A Unified Address is a single address that can carry more than one receiver type. We first added support for them in August 2025.[Read about it here.](https://www.gemini.com/blog/privacy-made-simple-gemini-adds-zcash-unified-addresses)


For the technical readers: the shielded part of a Unified Address is an Orchard receiver. Since NU6.3, new payments to that receiver land in Ironwood. That is how the protocol works (see ZIP 326). For you, the address is the same. You just copy, paste, and send.


### What This Means for You


- **Deposit from a shielded wallet:** Send ZEC from a compatible shielded wallet to your Gemini-issued shielded Unified Address.
- **Transparent addresses are still available:** If your wallet needs a transparent address, you can choose one.
- **Withdrawals work as before:** Gemini already supports withdrawals to shielded addresses.


### Why This Matters


Until now, the flow had a gap. You could withdraw ZEC from Gemini to a shielded address. But to send it back, you had to use a transparent deposit address.


That meant one half of the trip was private and the other half was not.


Shielded deposits fix that. If you hold ZEC in a compatible shielded wallet, you can send it straight to Gemini. No detour. No extra step. Privacy is the default, not something you have to work around.


To be clear: Shielded transfers protect your transaction details on the public blockchain. They do not guarantee anonymity from Gemini. Your account and compliance requirements do not change.


That is the right model. Privacy from the public. Clear rules for the platform.


### Gemini’s History With Zcash


Gemini originally listed ZEC in 2018, as the first licensed Zcash exchange. We added shielded withdrawals in 2020.


[In August 2025, we added unified address support](https://www.gemini.com/blog/privacy-made-simple-gemini-adds-zcash-unified-addresses) , then Orchard in November. This summer, we supported Ironwood, Orchard's replacement, on day one. In September 2026, we moved our Zcash infrastructure to Zakura.[Read more here.](https://www.gemini.com/blog/gemini-preps-for-faster-zcash-with-move-to-zakura)


Each step made private payments a little easier to use and a little stronger underneath. Shielded deposits are the next one.
